questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stop feeling tired at work
Why sleep is so important and what happens without it
Why some animals sleep in the day
How to fall asleep quickly
questions.why: They find out more about the benefits of sleep and what happens when you get too little.

questions.q: Why doesn't Phil answer Georgie at the start?
options: He is on the phone
He has gone home early because he isn't feeling very well today
He can't hear her
He is asleep because he slept badly the night before
questions.why: Phil admits he was sleeping because he didn't sleep well last night.

questions.q: What does Georgie say about people who get enough sleep?
options: They live about five years longer
They earn more money because they work better
They never get ill
They need less food
questions.why: She says they live about five years longer than people who don't.

questions.q: Why does Georgie mention that sleeping leaves us vulnerable to danger?
options: To warn people not to sleep outside
To explain why people have nightmares
To suggest that the benefits of sleep must be huge
To show that humans need much less sleep than most other animals
questions.why: She says going unconscious every night can only make sense if the benefits are huge.

questions.q: According to science journalist Ginny Smith, what happens after a bad night's sleep?
options: We remember new things better because we're more relaxed
We feel more creative
We find it hard to concentrate and learn new things
We need to eat more
questions.why: She says you just can't concentrate, and your brain isn't ready to take in new information.

questions.q: What does the brain do with new information while we sleep?
options: It moves it from short-term to long-term memory
It deletes most of it
It turns it into dreams and then forgets it by the morning
It stops working completely
questions.why: Ginny says the brain consolidates it, taking it 'from short-term storage to long-term storage'.

questions.q: What does Ginny say about the advice to 'sleep on' a problem?
options: It's just an old saying that has no scientific truth in it at all
It only works for children
It makes problems worse
It's true – the brain can work out problems during the night
questions.why: She says your brain works on things during the night, and you can wake up having solved the problem.

questions.q: What can long-term lack of sleep lead to, according to Ginny?
options: Better survival skills
A weaker immune system and other health problems
Stronger muscles
Needing less and less sleep as your body gets used to it
questions.why: She says chronic sleep deprivation can mean a damped-down immune system and knock-on problems.
